I have been doing this for 30 years on this same land. I know what it needs.

My 8 mu all go through the same rotation — wheat in winter, maize after harvest in summer. That is how everyone here farms. It works. I am not changing that.

For wheat, I will plant in October like always. I buy the improved seed from the village cooperative — the kind the township extension station recommends. Not the cheap unbranded seed and not the expensive hybrid varieties some younger farmers try. The improved seed has been reliable. I put down compound fertilizer before planting, then top-dress urea at jointing. I irrigate four times: once before sowing to prepare the seedbed, once in winter to protect roots from freezing, once at jointing, once at heading. My well is deep but it holds. I spray herbicide early and fungicide when I see powdery mildew starting on the neighbors' fields — I do not wait until I see it on mine.

For maize, I plant straight into the wheat stubble in June, no extra plowing — saves fuel and time, and my son who drives the tractor is busy with his city job in summer anyway. I use hybrid seed, same brand I have bought for the past several years, Xianyu type. Heavy nitrogen at the big bell stage, that is when maize needs it most. I irrigate at tasseling and grain fill if rain is short. I spray herbicide once right after emergence and check for corn borer in August.

Six mouths to feed and some income from off-farm work, so I am not gambling. I do what I know gives a steady harvest.
